# Sink and pull-down faucet — mechanism validation

**Status: force-tested simulation with explicit physical priors; not a calibrated sim-to-real match.** The photographed faucet's manufacturer, component weights, breakaway forces, hose stroke and valve type are unknown. No hand actuation of the faucet was observed. Passing these tests establishes numerical behavior under the specified assumptions, not agreement with an instrumented real faucet. This distinction is essential when using this asset for policy transfer.

## Files and reproduction

- `mjcf/faucet.xml` is standalone with `meshdir="meshes"`; copy the entire `mjcf` directory to relocate it. No Python controller is needed in MuJoCo.
- `params.py` is the editable parameter source. `build.py` uses a frozen copy of the supplied Blender OBJ parts in `evidence/source_assets`, with their original metadata. Upstream assets were not overwritten. `evidence/build_manifest.json` records hashes, all body COMs, principal moments and principal-frame quaternions.
- Run `python build.py`, then `python tests/run_all.py`, with the supplied MuJoCo 3.5 environment. The tests use `unittest`, NumPy and Torch; `pytest` is unnecessary. Results and sampled traces are in `tests/results.json` and `tests/traces.json`.
- Run `MUJOCO_GL=egl python review.py`, followed by `python plot_review.py` in an environment with Matplotlib and Pillow. `review.jpg` contains rest, half/full opening, mechanism detail and simulation force/travel plots. Separate PNGs and a vector PDF are in `evidence`.
- Reset with `mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(model, data, model.key('rest').id)`. The required key name `rest` is the only named object without the `faucet_` prefix. It sets the dock adhesion control to **1**. Plain `mj_resetData` leaves control zero and disables the magnet. Keep control at 1 during interaction, including extraction: contact itself gates the attraction.

This delivery remains in the explicitly requested mechanism folder. It consumes existing capture evidence; it does not create a new capture, reconstruction, website publication or online estimator. All tests and review images are offline. Render/test wall times are recorded separately; no real-time performance claim is made.

## Dimensions, registration and evidence

The frame is right-handed, +z up. Its xy origin is the bottom-centre projection of the sink bounds; z=0 is the lowest valve-housing surface in the assembled rest pose. The sink's original canonical frame is translated by `(0,0,0.32)` m. Its original WORLD mapping is `(1.212,-0.2375,0.5018)` m plus yaw **-90 degrees** for the whole assembly. The faucet's existing bottom-centre frame is placed at `(0.05459,0.12922,0.52520)` m in this assembly. The faucet dimensions are retained, rather than replacing it with a generic product.

| Quantity | Value | Evidence / confidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Faucet visual width × depth × height | 285.18 × 267.56 × 413.00 mm | Existing Blender `model.json`; height and reach fitted to two-view rays, not a ruler measurement |
| Spout centreline reach | 248 mm | Existing 124 mm radius arch; projected direction `(0.535,-0.845,0)` |
| Escutcheon | 255 × 66 mm | Existing asset; observed steel base plate |
| Head length / largest diameter | 108 / 50 mm | Existing mesh; approximate reflective surface reconstruction |
| Sink visual bounds | 885 × 577 × 204.2 mm | Existing two-basin asset fitted to layout cutouts |
| Source countertop WORLD z | 1.025 m | `layout/structure.json` |
| Triangulated faucet top WORLD z | 1.43401 m | Frames f0082/f0168; ray residual 0.965 mm is triangulation consistency, **not** total dimensional uncertainty |
| Top above source mounting z=1.027 | 407.01 mm | Approximate independent comparison with 413 mm asset height; 6 mm difference |
| Depth CLI check at f0168 (399,284) | WORLD `(1.49014,-0.42662,1.38704)` m | Re-ran `ktools point`; reflective depth differs from triangulation by 47 mm in z |
| Metric uncertainty | approximately 4% stated by source | Supplied scale, not independently tape-calibrated; reflective surfaces can be worse |
| Extraction range | 0–508 mm | Published 20-inch hose analogue; actual faucet unmeasured |
| Swivel | ±150 degrees | Conservative assumed stop; actual unit might swivel continuously |
| Head wrist | ±45 degrees on each of two hinges | Assumed hose-end articulation, with physical neck/socket interference near docking |
| Flow / temperature | 0–34.38 / ±37.24 degrees | Source joint-range priors; no observed motion |
| Buttons | 0–2 mm | Source priors; neither button actuated in video |
| Shut-off knobs | 0–90 degrees | Quarter-turn valve analogue; valves are hidden and their type/placement are assumed |

The original asset is `assets/sink_faucet/sink_faucet`, with companion `sink_double_basin` and `sink_drain`. The requested constrained articulation file contains cabinetry motions, not a measured faucet trajectory. Relevant source measurements/layout entries are retained in `evidence/measurements.json`.

Published checks, retrieved 2026-10-12:

1. [Delta Trinsic 9159T specification](https://media.deltafaucet.com/SpecSheet/DSP-K-9159T-DST%20Rev%20H.pdf): 411 mm overall height and 241 mm reach provide a size analogue to this 413 mm / 248 mm asset. This is **not an identification** of the photographed faucet.
2. [Delta 9159-DST product](https://www.deltafaucet.com/kitchen/product/9159-DST.html?bvstate=pg%3A38%2Fct%3Aq): magnetic docking, 360-degree swivel and 20-inch retractable hose support the mechanism family. We retain a conservative ±150-degree assumed stop.
3. [Delta manufacturer support on 9159 family weight](https://es.deltafaucet.com/kitchen/product/9159-ARLS-DST.html?bvstate=pg%3A6%2Fct%3Aq): a 9159-CZ-DST is stated to weigh 6 lb, about 2.72 kg. This is an assembly reference, not measured component weights or proof that the photographed faucet weighs 2.72 kg.
4. [Kohler K-3372 specification](https://resources.kohler.com/onlinecatalog/pdf/1012587_4.pdf): 838 × 559 mm double bowl provides a dimensional sanity check. The reconstructed 885 × 577 mm basin differs; it has not been snapped to a different product's dimensions.
5. [BrassCraft quarter-turn stops](https://www.brasscraft.com/products/water-supplies/water-stops/14-turn-stops/): 90-degree operating travel. Torque and mass are not supplied by this source.
6. [MuJoCo 3.5 XML reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html): native adhesion, frictionloss, damping, soft limits and mesh inertia semantics.
7. [Isaac Lab actuator documentation](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/main/source/api/lab/isaaclab.actuators.html): custom actuator interface. The included adapter targets the 2.x interface and needs integration validation in the installed Isaac version.

## Mechanisms and physical justification

**Swivel:** vertical hinge at the original tower pivot. Static friction 0.18 Nm corresponds to roughly 0.73 N at 248 mm radius in a quasistatic calculation. Damping 0.08 Nms/rad represents O-ring and bearing drag; the force-ramp test includes inertia and velocity, hence a larger measured threshold. No centring spring is used.

**Hose:** a downward rail follows the swivel spout. `F_spring = -8(q + 0.75)` N, so retraction preload is 6 N and increases to 10.064 N at full travel. A real counterweight is approximately constant-force; this spring is an effective counterweight plus increasing hose-bending resistance. The 6 N preload corresponds to a 0.612 kg weight in an ideal 1:1 routing. The 0.12 kg rail armature is an independently assumed effective moving hose/counterweight inertia, **not a claim of a consistent explicit 1:1 counterweight assembly**. Hose friction 0.65 N and damping 5 Ns/m produce restrained return without oscillation. The head, buttons and carriage total 0.275 kg, so gravity supplies 2.698 N downward. The initial nonmagnetic quasistatic pull estimate is `6 + 0.65 - 2.698 = 3.952 N`. The fully extended estimate is 8.016 N before velocity-dependent resistance.

The exposed hose is a massless spatial tendon drawn between the exit and carriage; the rail supplies its physical response. There is no flexible hose collision, lateral hose bending, routing around objects or under-counter snagging. The long stroke can be reached after swivelling outside the basin; pulling straight downward over the basin naturally contacts its floor. The wrist adds orientation, not an unconstrained 3D head workspace.

**Dock magnet:** 8 N `adhesion` on `faucet_carriage`, whose only collision geom is the gasket. The striker/gasket explicit contact pair bypasses the normal parent-contact filter. Both use collision bit 2; the rest of the scene uses bit 1. Thus the adhesion cannot stick the spray head to the basin. Attraction is zero after loss of contact; no controller or equality switching is used. The analytical docked pull estimate is 11.952 N. Soft-contact margin and solver regularization affect the measured release. Unlike a real magnet, this model has no attraction across a millimetre-scale air gap: the counterweight must first restore contact.

**Wrist and socket:** two intersecting revolutes allow pitch and roll; each has 0.025 Nm friction, 0.025 Nms/rad damping, 0.04 Nm/rad weak centring and 1e-5 kgm² armature. A 9 mm radius neck meets a 12-piece open socket when near the dock. This is a geometric guide; it does not impose a hidden equality weld. Dock geometry is approximate, and large tilted return trajectories can jam rather than redock. Only the tested aligned return is validated.

**Flow lever:** the original +x lift axis did not correspond to lifting the lever tip; it is corrected to local +y. A 45 g lever replaces the original 147 g mass-fraction allocation. Friction 0.12 Nm holds a chosen setting. A weak 0.07 Nm/rad torsion spring with reference -0.08 rad biases the lever into the off stop. This is an **off-seat friction detent approximation**, not a mechanically modelled click or multi-stable cam. The lever stays lifted after release because friction exceeds spring/gravity torque over the tested travel. Temperature rotation retains the original vertical pivot with 0.16 Nm friction and no restoring spring. Its precise two-axis cartridge geometry remains uncertain.

**Sprayer buttons:** 4 g and 6 g sliding caps, spring 650 N/m with -0.5 mm reference (0.325 N preload), 0.15 N friction, 1.2 Ns/m damping and 1 g equivalent armature. The first stage has compliant travel; the second stage is the stiff 2 mm joint stop. They return on release. Spray/stream hydraulics and any real button toggle state are not simulated. No invented pop-open angle is reported; this asset has no door, lid or release latch. Separation distance and wrist angle are the relevant measurements.

**Baskets and sink:** the original drain parts are fixed waste fittings, not removable strainers. Those fittings remain fixed and two new 85 g open wire baskets have free joints. Each uses 16 upright ribs, two segmented perimeter rings, four crossed bottom wires and one central lift stem. Radius 35 mm, wall height 23 mm, wire radius 1.5 mm and stem height 30 mm are commodity-strainer priors, not observed basket measurements. Their rest-key placement has a small drop clearance; they settle under gravity. The 724-piece basin collision shell in the frozen source follows the rounded bowls and keeps both cavities and waste throats open. Source notes describe an earlier coarse floor decomposition; the frozen mesh manifest, not that stale prose, defines the delivered collisions.

**Valves:** two fixed brass housing proxies and 35 g quarter-turn knobs. The visible valve components are inferred behind the sink, with no measured plumbing registration. A 46 × 12 × 22 mm knob provides 23 mm grip radius. Friction 0.45 Nm implies 19.57 N tangential breakaway; damping 0.06 Nms/rad suppresses abrupt motion. These values represent a firm serviceable valve, not a seized or leaking one.

## Mass, inertia and contact model

All individual masses are **assumed component allocations**. No product source establishes this faucet's per-body masses. The above-deck assembly totals 1.785 kg, leaving about 0.94 kg relative to the 2.72 kg product analogue for hoses, fittings and a counterweight that are not explicitly meshed as moving rigid bodies. This is an accounting comparison, not a measured bill of materials. The original 2.1 kg assembly prior is not silently treated as ground truth. The fixed sink's 9 kg and fixed drain's 0.18 kg each are retained priors; their mass does not influence motion because they are anchored.

Inertia comes from MuJoCo's geometry integration, not a diagonal number chosen merely for stability. Mesh contact-piece masses are allocated by convex volume within each faucet part; spout capsule masses by length; basket masses by wire length. The sink's fixed total mass is split equally across its shell pieces. Mass-zero visual meshes are excluded from mass accumulation. Meshes use convex collision and their integrated moments; this approximates hollow metal/plastic parts with a uniform equivalent mass distribution. Hidden cartridge internals and head shell wall thickness are not reconstructed. Principal inertia/COM outputs are listed below and in the manifest.

Steel/polymer contact uses `(sliding, torsional, rolling) = (0.45, 0.002 m, 0.0001 m)`, a dry mixed-material engineering prior. Gasket/striker uses `(0.8, 0.002 m, 0.0001 m)` to represent rubber/steel traction. The explicit pair has two sliding coefficients of 0.8. General contacts use condim 4; the docking pair uses condim 3, so its torsional/rolling values are recorded but inactive. Wetness and contamination are not calibrated. Rendering uses satin steel, black polymer and brass colour/specular priors; optical reflectance is not measured.

Internal bearing overlaps are intentionally excluded for base–spout, base–yaw carrier and base–lever. Adjacent head/button parts use the ordinary parent filter; spout–button exclusions remove internal socket overlap. These exclusions model mating mechanisms, not external obstacles. The external head, baskets, bowls and dock remain contact-enabled. Visual spout vertices at the outlet are trimmed to remove the original tip/head overlap; the revised spout collision is an open curved capsule chain plus socket.

## Solver and parameter units

- Timestep 0.5 ms; implicitfast; 100 solver iterations; tolerance 1e-10; elliptic friction cone; gravity 9.81 m/s². The short step is required by stiff button/contact response.
- Contacts: `solref=(0.001 s,1)`, `solimp=(0.99,0.999,0.0005 m)`; margin 0.1 mm. These were tightened after the initial basket drop exceeded 2 mm penetration. They approximate near-rigid metal contact, not measured rubber compliance.
- Joint soft stops: `solreflimit=(0.006 s,1)`, `solimplimit=(0.95,0.99,0.001)`; width units match the joint. Button stops: `(0.002 s,1)` and `(0.95,0.99,0.0002 m)`. Small limit overtravel is intentional compliant response, not extra mechanical travel.
- Friction constraints: `solreffriction=(0.002 s,1)`, `solimpfriction=(0.9999,0.9999,0.001)`. High impedance reduces artificial low-load creep, especially in low-inertia valve knobs. Some regularized creep remains; finite-duration force ramps are not mathematical static-friction measurements.
- Rotational rows: frictionloss Nm; damping Nms/rad; armature kgm²; stiffness Nm/rad; reference/range radians. Linear rows: N, Ns/m, kg, N/m, metres respectively.
- Geometry numbers in the complete parameter listing are metres; colour/solver impedances are unitless except the explicitly stated solver widths. The site radius is a display aid, not a contact shape. Material/render/camera settings are visual-only choices in the builder/review script.
- To apply a future metric calibration, edit only `PARAMS['length_scale']` then rebuild. Mesh vertices, pivots, geoms, linear ranges, linear spring references, contact margins and relevant impedance widths rescale together. Body masses stay fixed; geometry-derived inertias scale as length squared. The nominal physical spring rates, friction, damping and armature are deliberately not automatically re-identified. Consequently preload changes with the scaled spring reference; recalibrate forces and rerun tests after a scale change.

## Isaac Lab port

`isaac/actuators.py` includes a `FaucetActuatorCfg`, custom actuator, joint property table and vectorized Torch force law. It carries the same springs, frictionloss, damping, armature, limits and contact-gated 8 N docking force. Supply the **filtered striker/gasket contact state and normal projection** and the estimated external generalized effort (including gravity, excluding the actuator itself) every physics substep. At low speed, the law cancels external drive up to Coulomb capacity; at speed it opposes velocity. Omitting the external-force estimate removes correct static hold under a hand load.

MuJoCo frictionloss is an absolute N/Nm bound; PhysX joint friction is not the same quantity. The port therefore sets native friction/damping to zero to prevent double counting and implements SI friction explicitly. PhysX compliant limits and the explicit penalty stop must not both be enabled. The fallback stop stiffness is 50,000 N/m / 200 Nm/rad, damping 10 Ns/m / 2 Nms/rad, stiction threshold 0.001 joint-units/s. These are approximation parameters, not equivalent MuJoCo solver coefficients. The adapter's effort cap is 1000 SI units and velocity cap 100 SI units, chosen as nonbinding interface bounds, not safe product limits. The complete XML limits remain required in the imported articulation.

Two pure-Torch law tests ran locally. **No Isaac/PhysX integration test was possible because Isaac Lab is not installed in the execution environment.** Native adhesion, collision filtering, imported inertia/armature behavior and static friction need cross-engine validation. The port must not be presented as a validated equivalent simulator.

## Required real-world calibration before sim-to-real claims

Identify the faucet and valve type; measure arch/lever/head dimensions with a ruler; weigh the removable head and basket; use a force gauge to pull at the specified grip points slowly in both directions; record the entire hose force–displacement curve and return time; measure flow/temperature/swivel breakaway and hysteresis. Check full wrist range and tilted redocking. Replace the stated priors with those measurements and compare independent repeats rather than accepting the model's own target ranges as evidence. Uncertainty is presently dominated by missing physical observations, not solver repeatability.

## Final validation results

**PASS: 10 tests (8 MuJoCo integration groups, 2 pure-Torch law tests).** MuJoCo 3.5.0. Test wall time 127.876 s; aggregate stepped simulation time across resets 53.160 s. This aggregate is not an online estimation benchmark. Review state simulation and rendering took 39.194 s.

The final XML SHA-256 is `2d8cdcc93d1622bde7ffdac54480de113baca9e3b53d2dee7a237b3940151ee3`. Checked 795 referenced convex mesh colliders: convex, watertight and positive volume = **True**. Analytic capsules, cylinders and boxes are convex by construction. Initial enabled contacts have no negative distance; the largest contact penetration across all integration trajectories is **0.5714 mm** (requirement: at most 2 mm). No NaN or MuJoCo warning occurred in passing runs. No claim is made about untested adversarial impacts.

Breakaway protocol: increase force by 0.25 N every 80 ms at the physical grip site using `xfrc_applied` and the force-to-COM moment arm. Motion threshold is 2 mm for extraction and 0.02 rad for rotary joints. These finite-rate thresholds depend on inertia, dwell and damping. Targets were selected as plausibility priors before the final run; they are not real-appliance measurements.
